_legal: PROGRESSION-ONLY. This file contains chord progressions (unprotectable functional harmony) and factual song titles. It contains NO riffs, NO melodies, NO lyrics, NO tab, NO transcribed arrangement. Nothing here was scraped from a tab site. Lessons teach the progression and say honestly which song uses it; they never teach the song's signature riff or melodic line. See AMENDMENT-12.
_schema: chords[] reference keys in ./shapes.json. mystery.* powers Mystery Mode: the student learns the loop blind, then the reveal names the song.

songs.title: Zombie
songs.honest_claim: This is the four-chord loop the whole song sits on. Play it and it is recognisable.

mystery.hint_1: Four chords. Irish band, early 90s. The whole song never leaves this loop.
mystery.hint_2: The chorus is one word, repeated.
mystery.reveal: That's the loop from 'Zombie' by The Cranberries (1994).

songs.title: Californication
songs.honest_claim: The verse and chorus both ride this loop. The famous single-note line sits on top of it - we are not teaching that line, just the harmony under it.
teaches: vi-IV-I-V - the most common loop in pop music

mystery.hint_1: Four chords, minor start. You have heard this exact loop in a hundred other songs.
mystery.hint_2: California. 1999. Bass player is more famous than the chords.
mystery.reveal: That's the loop from 'Californication' by Red Hot Chili Peppers (1999).

songs.title: Sweet Home Alabama
songs.feel: loose southern shuffle, accent the 2 and 4
songs.honest_claim: Three chords, round and round, the entire song. The intro lick is separate and we do not teach it.
teaches: three-chord loop with no minor chords

mystery.hint_1: Three chords. Southern rock. It never changes.
mystery.hint_2: There is a state in the title.
mystery.reveal: That's the loop from 'Sweet Home Alabama' by Lynyrd Skynyrd (1974).

songs.title: Highway to Hell
songs.feel: hard, short, stabbed chords - silence between them
songs.honest_claim: This is the harmony the riff is built from. We teach the chords and a generic stab rhythm; the recorded riff's specific timing and articulation stay off-limits.

mystery.hint_1: Three chords, but the space between them is the point.
mystery.reveal: That's the harmony behind 'Highway to Hell' by AC/DC (1979).

songs.title: Johnny B. Goode
songs.feel: straight-eight rock and roll, drive it
songs.honest_claim: This is the 12-bar blues form - a public, long-standing structure (over a century old), not anyone's property. Thousands of songs use it. The song's lead intro is separate and not taught.

mystery.hint_1: Twelve bars. Three chords. This form is older than rock and roll and built it.
mystery.hint_2: 1958. The most copied intro in history - which you are not playing.
mystery.reveal: That's the 12-bar form under 'Johnny B. Goode' by Chuck Berry (1958) - and under a thousand blues songs.

songs.title: The House of the Rising Sun
songs.loop: Am - C - D - F - Am - C - E - E
songs.honest_claim: FULLY PUBLIC DOMAIN. This one is a traditional folk song - we can teach the melody, the words, and the traditional arrangement freely. The only song on this list where that is true.

mystery.hint_1: Five chords in a minor key, rolling in threes. Older than every other song here.
mystery.hint_2: New Orleans. A house. Nobody owns it.
mystery.reveal: That's 'The House of the Rising Sun' - traditional, public domain, yours to play and record freely.

songs.title: Nothing Else Matters
songs.feel: slow, quiet, let each chord ring
songs.honest_claim: The verse harmony. The fingerpicked intro figure is a composed riff and is deliberately NOT taught here.

mystery.hint_1: Three chords, descending, very slow, very quiet.
mystery.hint_2: The loudest band in the world wrote it. 1991.
mystery.reveal: That's the verse harmony of 'Nothing Else Matters' by Metallica (1991).

songs.title: Back In Black
songs.honest_claim: The three chords the song is built on. The riff that decorates them is the copyrighted part and is not taught.

mystery.hint_1: Three chords. Same band as one you have already learned.
mystery.hint_2: 1980. An album cover with nothing on it.
mystery.reveal: That's the harmony behind 'Back In Black' by AC/DC (1980).

songs.title: Wish You Were Here
songs.loop: Em - G - Em - G - Em - A7 - Em - A7 - G - C - D - C - G
songs.honest_claim: The verse harmony. The famous opening lead line is a composed melody and is not taught.

mystery.hint_1: It breathes. Long chords, lots of space, a dominant 7th that aches.
mystery.hint_2: 1975. A handshake and a man on fire.
mystery.reveal: That's the verse harmony of 'Wish You Were Here' by Pink Floyd (1975).

songs.title: Stairway to Heaven
songs.loop: Am - C - D - F - Am - C - G - D
songs.feel: gentle arpeggios, one note at a time
songs.honest_claim: The chord movement under the intro. The picked figure itself is the single most litigated riff in rock - we do not teach it, and we do not reproduce it.

mystery.hint_1: Minor, climbing, five chords. Famously banned in guitar shops.
mystery.hint_2: 1971. Eight minutes long, and it starts this quietly.
mystery.reveal: That's the chord movement under the intro of 'Stairway to Heaven' by Led Zeppelin (1971).
